title: Duplicated signer-resolution logic in CRL check methods
description:
Location: pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs, check_revocation() (lines 466-690) and check_revocation_against_anchor() (lines 718-871)

The two RevocationChecker trait methods on CrlChecker share ~150 lines of nearly-identical logic:
1. parse_issuing_dp + indirect-CRL flag resolution (5-arm match on crl_issuer_cert x crl_declares_indirect)
2. CRL issuer name match
3. cRLSign check
4. Validity window check
5. Signature verification
6. IDP scope check
7. Delta CRL merge
8. check_revocation_status_indirect call

The only substantive difference is the identity source (issuer Certificate vs TrustAnchor) for steps 1-3. A private method taking an abstract (subject: &Name, spki: SubjectPublicKeyInfoRef, signer_cert: Option<&Certificate>) tuple would eliminate the duplication. The current code acknowledges this implicitly by numbering both methods' steps identically (1-7 / 1-8).

What goes wrong: any bug fix or behavioral change (e.g., adding a new IDP scope flag check) must be applied to both methods in lockstep. The methods are already ~400 lines of dense RFC logic; missing a parallel update is a plausible future bug source.
